condition: progressive bilateral dorsal hand depigmented patches over 6 months in a young adult man with dark brown skin
level_rationale: Six months of progressively expanding smooth depigmented chalk-white patches across the backs of both hands in a 24-year-old man with dark brown skin indicates active acral vitiligo warranting dermatologist evaluation with Wood's lamp examination and targeted topical immunomodulator or phototherapy treatment, whereas developing a slight even sun tan across the backs of both hands over 6 months reflects normal physiological tanning requiring no medical care.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 24 year old man with dark brown skin
Skin change has developed on the backs of both hands over 6 months
Smooth chalk white patches of lost skin pigment have kept spreading

everyday_sources.evidence: Both of my hands were affected, my legs, parts of my face, my arms, my genital area, my torso, my feet, yeah, everything started getting white patches with time, and every time it was faster and faster.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain darker-skin young-adult male everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + unsourced sun-damage causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact dorsal-hand pigment de-escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (24-year-old man with dark brown skin, 6-month history on the backs of both hands, and spreading smooth chalk-white patches) without naming vitiligo, with a 1-word span difference (16 vs 17 words), orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, overriding plan.json's multi-organ mucosal-fever bundle to change only the pigment property on the backs of both hands in f3 from spreading chalk-white patches to a slight even sun tan shifts care cleanly from dermatologist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
